course_name_original: The Anthropology of Everyday Life. From Birth to Death
course_name_en: The Anthropology of Everyday Life. From Birth to Death

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows and understands basic anthropological terms.
Student knows the history of changes in birth, wedding, and funeral customs over the last century. Learns the specifics of the research methodology of a historian and ethnologist.
Student can independently search for sources to study customs.
Student can independently formulate a research problem and interpret it in the form of an essay.

syllabus_topics: How was it? - a few words about searching for ethnographic and historical sources. Basic concepts used in ethnology and anthropology: custom, habit, ritual, ceremony, tradition, superstitions, apotropaic measures. Family rituals: birth, wedding, funeral. Customary changes in the last century. Traditional rituals and contemporary ceremonies. The word in ritual and ceremony (granting goods through words, i.e., the ritual of blessing in traditional culture). Genres, functions, and transformations of songs: lullabies, wedding songs, and funeral songs. Instruments, musicians, funeral singers. Genre photography: changes in aesthetics, theme, form.
